It never asked about or confirmed CO symptoms: there was no callback, and the SMS only gives conditional advice ('if anyone has a headache... leave'). The agent itself lists unconfirmed symptoms as missing information and puts 'Confirm with tenant that no symptoms' under remaining work. So it treated the case as non-emergency without confirming there were no symptoms.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled this well: it identified the sealed, end-of-life unit, put responsibility on the landlord, told the tenant not to remove or disable the alarm, gave clear emergency advice and logged the fan separately. Its main gap is that it never confirmed the absence of CO symptoms before treating the case as non-emergency. It also held the alarm job for landlord approval even though the cost was under the spend limit.
